authority: PI, 2026-09-03, signing off on the tier structure with one wording correction
PURPOSE: Deployment-only (inference-time, no retraining) robustness testing across three disturbance families, at low/medium/high severity plus a nominal zero-disturbance condition, applied to trained latent-conditioned policies at each team size (2v2/4v4/6v6).

localization_noise.mechanism: gpu_env sensor_noise_sigma_cells (existing config field, currently unused -- defaults to 0.0 in every training run this program has performed)
localization_noise.precedent: 0.12 matches this codebase's own existing domain-randomization ceiling, dr_sensor_noise_sigma_max

motion_error.mechanism: gpu_env drift_sigma_cells (existing config field, currently unused -- defaults to 0.0). Confirmed by reading gpu_env/_core/_dynamics.py: adds Gaussian noise directly to the post-motion position after the commanded velocity integrates -- i.e., realized displacement differs from commanded displacement, exactly the definition of motion error.
motion_error.why_same_numbers_as_localization_noise: MATCHED-SCALE TEST LEVELS, not a claim of equivalent severity. Localization and motion error share units, so using the same numeric ladder makes the robustness suite easy to interpret as one matrix. This is a controlled matched-scale perturbation choice, not an assumption that motion error has a known physical ceiling of its own -- unlike localization noise, no domain-randomization precedent exists for drift_sigma_cells in this codebase, so equal numeric values were chosen deliberately for comparability, not derived independently.
motion_error.PAPER_CAVEAT_REQUIRED: 0.12 cells localization noise != 0.12 cells motion error in behavioral severity. Localization corrupts what the agent believes is true; motion drift corrupts what physically happens after it acts. Frozen caption sentence: "For localization and motion perturbations, we use a matched numeric severity schedule of 0.03, 0.06, and 0.12 cells to enable controlled comparison across perturbation families. These levels are not assumed to represent equivalent behavioral difficulty."

control_delay.mechanism: NOT YET IMPLEMENTED. Requires a new action-buffer wrapper in the eval rollout loop only (no training-loop involvement) -- delays the policy's selected action by N ticks before the environment executes it.
control_delay.simulator_resolution: decision_interval_seconds = 0.5 -- each simulator tick IS 0.5 real seconds (gpu_env/_config.py). Literal sub-tick delay (e.g. a few milliseconds) is not representable at this discretization; tiers are chosen in whole ticks rather than inventing sub-tick precision.

nominal_baseline.rule: a zero-disturbance condition (all three mechanisms at their existing 0.0 default) is retained for every team size and every method, as the reference every low/medium/high tier is compared against.

DEPLOYMENT_ONLY_GUARANTEE.localization_noise: structurally deployment-only -- sensor_noise_sigma_cells is read at rollout time by the observation model; setting it only for eval invocations cannot leak into training, since training runs never pass a nonzero value
DEPLOYMENT_ONLY_GUARANTEE.motion_error: structurally deployment-only, same reasoning -- drift_sigma_cells is read at rollout time in the dynamics step
DEPLOYMENT_ONLY_GUARANTEE.control_delay: will be implemented as an eval-only wrapper around action selection in the rollout loop, never touching the training loop -- to be verified by a preflight check once built, matching this program's standing discipline of proving rather than asserting deployment-only guarantees

TEST_MATRIX: 3 disturbance families x 3 severities (+ 1 nominal baseline) x N team sizes x M methods x K seeds per cell -- exact N/M/K to be fixed when the team-size training entrypoint and evaluation seed blocks are frozen
NEXT: build the control-delay eval wrapper, freeze its own deployment-only preflight, then build the robustness-suite runner that sweeps all three families at all three tiers against whichever checkpoints exist per team size
